summary.title: Get your work recognized: write a brag document
summary.one_liner: Keep a running "brag document" of your accomplishments, impact, and learning so you can remember and clearly communicate your work at performance review time.
keywords: what did i do this year
takeaways: Maintain a brag document listing projects, contributions, and their impact, since you and your manager both forget much of what you did.
Share the document with your manager and peer reviewers to make it easier for them to advocate for you.
Include fuzzy, hard-to-quantify work and explain its goal, actions taken, and effects, and describe the impact of each item rather than just the action.
Use the document to spot patterns in your work, such as themes, what you are proud of, and what you want to do more or less of.
Template sections include projects, collaboration and mentorship, design and documentation, company building, what you learned, outside-of-work activities, and goals.
summary.summary: The author explains why engineers forget their accomplishments at review time and why managers cannot advocate well without help, then proposes keeping a "brag document." She covers sharing it with managers and peer reviewers, using it to reflect on patterns and fuzzy work, and two group formats: a brag workshop and biweekly writing sessions. The post ends with a detailed template organized into projects, collaboration, design docs, company building, learning, outside work, and prompts. It is written as a practical personal and team practice rather than a tool or framework.
